claims.text: Always image with more than transiently impaired consciousness, GCS < 15, focal findings, persistent vomiting, seizures, loss of consciousness, or a suspected fracture.
claims.quote: Imaging should always be done in patients with more than transiently impaired consciousness, GCS score < 15, focal neurologic findings, persistent vomiting, seizures, a history of loss of consciousness, or clinically suspected fractures.

claims.text: Possibly not needed after brief loss of consciousness (< 5 seconds) or transient amnesia in a patient who is alert with GCS 15.
claims.quote: Some evidence suggests that CT is not necessary in patients with brief loss of consciousness (ie, < 5 seconds) or transient amnesia or disorientation but who are alert with a GCS of 15 during examination.

claims.text: Canadian CT Head Rule is for minor head injury: loss of consciousness, amnesia or confusion, with a GCS score of at least 13–15.
claims.quote: The definition of “minor head injury” used when deriving this rule included “a history of loss of consciousness (LOC), amnesia or confusion as well as a GCS score of at least 13–15”

claims.text: High risk: GCS not 15 within 2 hours, suspected open skull fracture, any sign of basal skull fracture, vomiting ≥ 2 episodes, or age ≥ 65 years.
claims.quote: five high-risk factors (“failure to reach a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 15 within 2 hours, suspected open skull fracture, any sign of basal skull fracture, vomiting ≥2 episodes or age ≥65 years”)

claims.text: Medium risk: amnesia before impact > 30 minutes, or a dangerous mechanism of injury.
claims.quote: two medium-risk factors (“amnesia before impact >30min and dangerous mechanism of injury”)

claims.text: CT only with any one of these findings; the rule doesn't apply to patients on anticoagulants or with bleeding disorders.
claims.quote: CT Head is only required for mild head injury patients with any one of these findings—Rule is not applicable for patients on anticoagulants or with bleeding disorders.
claims.locator: Table 1, Canadian CT head rule criteria

claims.text: Children: the PECARN algorithm helps limit radiation from head CT.
claims.quote: For children with head injury, the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) has developed an algorithm that may help limit radiation exposure from head CT

claims.text: Epidural hematoma on CT: lenticular hyperdensity over the middle meningeal artery.
claims.quote: CT: Hyperdensity in epidural space, classically lenticular-shaped and located over the middle meningeal artery (temporal fossa) due to a temporal bone fracture

claims.text: Subdural hematoma on CT: crescent-shaped hyperdensity.
claims.quote: CT: Hyperdensity in subdural space, classically crescent-shaped
